transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-10-15 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Tom Reynolds (Redwood AE), Aisha Patel (Redwood SE), Evan Martinez (Celestia Head of IT Security), Priya Singh (CTO), Marta Lopez (Compliance Manager)

Summary: quick run through of audit logging capabilities focused on admin activity capture, export/integrations, retention, and encryption/KMS. Lots of detailed SIEM integration questions from Evan. Agreed to send artifacts and sample logs.

[00:00] Tom: Okay, thanks everyone for joining, we'll keep to 45 minutes. quick intros, uh, I'm Tom from Redwood, this is Aisha our security/infra SE.
[00:18] Aisha: Hi all, thanks. We'll cover what audit logs capture, how you can export them, retention defaults, and options for CMEK and regional retention. Feel free to jump in.
[00:32] Evan: Sounds good. We're mostly interested in admin activity — who did what, when — and making sure we can ship those to our SIEM, and that retention matches our PCI and regional rules.
[00:47] Priya: Also need assurance on where logs live, like EU only, and whether admin logs ever contain cardholder data or full request payloads.
[00:58] Marta: and SOC2 evidence — we need to see actual audit artifacts and change history for a sample window.

[02:03] Aisha: Great, high level: Redwood splits logs into control-plane/admin activity logs and data-plane logs. Admin logs capture actor (user/service account), action (create, update, delete, role-change, auth events), target resource, timestamp, source IP, user-agent, request id, outcome (success/failure), and a concise change_summary. We do not store raw PII or full user-submitted content in admin logs.
[02:38] Evan: change_summary — is that the delta? like previous state vs new?
[02:44] Aisha: It's a short delta when feasible — for config changes we'll record previous and new values for non-sensitive fields. sensitive fields are redacted. e.g., if an API key rotated we log that a key rotation occurred but not the key value.
[02:58] Tom: Also note we capture role-assignment events, SSO/SAML provisioning actions, SCIM user create/delete, MFA status changes, and KMS key assignment events.

[04:10] Priya: How granular are timestamps? we need millisecond-level tracing to correlate with our traces.
[04:17] Aisha: We provide epoch millis timestamps and a request_id per call that you can use to stitch logs to your application traces.

[05:05] Evan: Ok good. Now about export — we have Splunk on-prem, Datadog cloud, and long-run S3 buckets for archives. What's supported?
[05:15] Aisha: Multiple options: near-real-time streaming via Kafka or Kinesis connectors, S3 archival (JSON/NDJSON) with configurable lifecycle policies, syslog forwarding, and native connectors to Splunk HEC and Datadog Logs API. You can also pull logs using Redwood's audit-logs REST API (paginated, filters by actor/action/time).
[05:45] Evan: For S3 dumps, are files signed or checksummed? we need integrity verification for forensics.
[05:52] Tom: Yes, exports support checksums (SHA256) and optionally signed manifests. For streaming we support message signing/HMAC and TLS mutual auth for ingestion endpoints.

[07:02] Marta: Retention — what's default and what's available for enterprise? we may need 7 years for some records.
[07:09] Aisha: Default retention for audit logs is 90 days for standard hosted customers. For enterprise we offer custom retention up to multi-year: 1, 3, 7 years, etc. Longer retention is implemented via archival to your S3 or Redwood-managed archival with CMEK. We can also set tiered retention—hot for 90 days, then archive.

[08:10] Evan: If we ask for 7 years, does Redwood keep logs compressed and encrypted with our keys?
[08:17] Aisha: Yes — we support customer-managed keys (CMEK) using AWS KMS, and for on-prem or higher security customers HSM integrations. When logs are archived to S3 we can encrypt them with your KMS key. For Redwood-managed archival we still allow CMEK.

[09:05] Priya: Data residency: can audit logs be stored only in EU region? we have EEA-only rules.
[09:12] Tom: Yes — Redwood has regional logging options. For Private/Dedicated deployments we can ensure logs remain in EU region; for hosted customers we have EU data regions and a regional export pipeline so data does not leave region. We'll include specifics in the follow-up doc.

[10:30] Evan: Is there a way to stream admin events to our SIEM in near real time for monitoring?
[10:36] Aisha: You can stream events via Kafka/Kinesis or push them to your Splunk HEC endpoint or Datadog intake. We also provide webhooks for critical alerts. Latency depends on pipeline; typical end-to-end is sub-5s for our streaming offering.

[11:55] Marta: Compliance evidence: can you show us sample logs with the fields we mentioned for SOC2 audit? redacted is fine.
[12:03] Tom: Yes, we'll send a redacted sample set and the mapping doc that explains each field and retention decisions.

[13:10] Evan: Aisha, on the schema — what does a single admin event look like? can you give an example?
[13:17] Aisha: Sure — JSON event includes: event_id, timestamp (ms), actor {type,user_id,source_ip}, action, resource_type, resource_id, outcome, request_id, user_agent, change_summary, policy_id (if applicable). we'll show an example in the export sample.

[14:45] Priya: Do audit logs ever include the text of the request payload or customer content? that would be a no for PCI.
[14:52] Aisha: By default no — admin logs do not contain user-submitted content or PII. Data plane traces are separate and by default we do not log full content. If you need more detailed diagnostics we can enable obfuscated/controlled payload capture in a private deployment under strict controls.

[16:12] Evan: What about RBAC and attribution — if a change is made by an automation service account, can we see the originating principal and role?
[16:20] Aisha: Yes we capture the principal (service account or human), the role/permission set in effect, and any SCIM group sync events. That allows you to map effective permissions at the time of change.

[17:00] Marta: Audit trail for policy changes — do you keep who changed a policy, when, and can we rollback or at least see previous policy blob?
[17:08] Aisha: We keep a change history with previous blob metadata for non-sensitive policy fields; for full rollback we can provide the previous config object in logs (again redacting secrets).

[18:30] Evan: Integration security — how do you authenticate the stream to our Splunk? do you use token, certs?
[18:37] Aisha: Splunk HEC uses token-based auth; for direct syslog you can use mutual TLS. For Kafka/Kinesis we support IAM-based auth and mTLS. We also offer signed payloads.

[19:40] Priya: Are logs queryable from the console for admins? and is that exposed to RBAC controls?
[19:47] Tom: Yes, we have an audit log viewer with search and filters, and access is controlled by RBAC. You can scope who can view or export logs; exports themselves are gated.

[20:50] Evan: We're also concerned about tamper evidence — can you attest logs weren't changed?
[20:58] Aisha: For archival we provide signed manifests and checksums. For high-assurance customers we can enable append-only storage with cryptographic chains plus periodic signed snapshots for tamper evidence.

[22:15] Marta: How long do you keep console UI activity logs vs API logs, are both treated the same?
[22:22] Aisha: We capture both UI and API admin events. They are stored in the same audit pipeline; retention policies apply equally, but you can choose to only export API or UI events if desired.

[23:40] Evan: Is there a live demo for setting up SSO/SAML and checking audit events? maybe a quick run-through in our tenant.
[23:46] Tom: Yes we can do a tenant walk-through; next step will include SSO docs and a dates for a session.

[25:10] Priya: If we use Private deployment, does logging change? do we get direct access to raw logs?
[25:18] Aisha: In Private/Dedicated you get more control — direct access to raw log files, ability to deploy your own collectors, and full CMEK/HSM options. Also you can push logs internally without crossing public networks if required.

[27:00] Evan: For forensic requests, can we request a replay of events with full context within a time window?
[27:07] Aisha: Yes — we support replay/export for specified windows; for long windows we typically stage an S3 export and provide checksums and manifests.

[28:30] Marta: Are there limits on export size or rate? we have heavy event volumes during deployments.
[28:37] Aisha: We can handle high throughput; for very large volumes we recommend streaming connectors (Kafka/Kinesis). There are per-tenant rate limits on the REST export API but streaming has essentially unbounded throughput within allocated capacity. We'll include expected throughput numbers in follow-up.

[30:00] Evan: About retention deletion: if we purge logs per retention, is there any residual copy left? we need guarantee of deletion for data minimization.
[30:10] Aisha: Deletion is deterministic — once retention expires logs are removed from hot storage and marked for deletion in archive; for Redwood-managed archival we remove all copies per the schedule. If you use customer S3, you control lifecycle. We'll provide documentation on our deletion guarantees.

[31:40] Priya: Encryption at rest — is metadata also encrypted and does indexing create plaintext copies?
[31:46] Aisha: Metadata and payload are encrypted at rest. Our indexing pipeline keeps indexes encrypted and access-controlled; sensitive fields are masked prior to indexing when requested.

[33:05] Evan: Do you support SCIM provisioning so when we disable a user it's clear in the audit?
[33:11] Aisha: Yes SCIM events are logged and we capture the lifecycle (create/update/delete, disable).

[34:20] Marta: For audits, we need a signed log subset for the auditor. can you provide that?
[34:27] Tom: Yes — we can provide signed manifests and a zipped export of the timeframe you need, along with mapping docs.

[35:50] Evan: Any gotchas around PII? is there any chance content gets slipped into logs during errors?
[35:57] Aisha: Rarely; our runtime generally separates customer payloads from control events. For error cases we have rules to scrub payloads; we can set tighter scrubbing for Celestia. We'll show the scrubbing rules.

[37:10] Priya: Network/IP whitelisting for log push — can we limit egress to our IPs?
[37:16] Aisha: Yes, for streaming endpoints we support IP allowlists and mutual TLS.

[38:30] Tom: quick recap of next steps — we'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts, redacted sample logs + schema, SSO/SAML docs, and proposed pricing for retention. Aisha will follow up with SIEM connector instructions.

[39:00] Evan: Great, thanks. one more: can you include examples for Splunk queries using the event fields you described?
[39:06] Aisha: Yes we'll include Splunk and Datadog query examples.

[40:10] Marta: timeline — we'd like the artifacts this week so we can pass to our auditor.
[40:15] Tom: we'll aim to get materials by tomorrow EOD, worst case Friday.

[41:30] Priya: if everything looks good we may spin up a pilot to validate ingestion and retention in our environment.
[41:36] Tom: excellent. we'll coordinate the pilot details in the follow-up.

[43:00] (wrap-up) Tom: thanks everyone, we'll send the packet and set up the technical deep dive.
[43:07] Evan: thanks all.
[43:10] End of transcript (light transcription artifacts present; some names/terms auto-corrected).
